title: ECB invites expressions of interest for digital euro innovation workstreams
summary: The European central Bank is inviting private companies and organisations to join the digital euro innovation platform to collaborate on experiments with new value-added services and explore future technological developments.
content: The European Central Bank has invited private companies and organizations to submit expressions of interest to join its digital euro innovation platform. Participants will collaborate on experiments exploring new value-added services and future technological developments related to the digital euro project.
content_ta: European Central Bank தனது digital euro innovation platform-ல் இணைய விருப்பமுள்ள தனியார் நிறுவனங்கள் மற்றும் அமைப்புகளுக்கு அழைப்பு விடுத்துள்ளது. digital euro திட்டம் தொடர்பான புதிய மதிப்புக்கூட்டு சேவைகள் மற்றும் எதிர்கால தொழில்நுட்ப வளர்ச்சிகள் குறித்த பரிசோதனைகளில் பங்கேற்பாளர்கள் இணைந்து செயல்படுவார்கள்.

title: NEAR Intents says it blocked $50M tied to Bitget hackers
summary: The cross-chain protocol said it actively prevents stolen funds from being laundered, drawing a contrast with THORChain’s position that it does not selectively censor transactions.
content: NEAR Intents announced it successfully blocked fifty million dollars tied to the Bitget hackers. The cross-chain protocol stated that it actively prevents stolen funds from being laundered. This approach contrasts sharply with THORChain, which maintains a policy of not selectively censoring transactions on its network.
content_ta: Bitget ஹேக்கர்களுடன் தொடர்புடைய 50 மில்லியன் டாலர்களை வெற்றிகரமாகத் தடுத்ததாக NEAR Intents அறிவித்துள்ளது. திருடப்பட்ட நிதியை வெள்ளையாக்குவதை (laundering) தாங்கள் தீவிரமாகத் தடுப்பதாக அந்த க்ராஸ்-செயின் புரோட்டோகால் தெரிவித்துள்ளது. தன் நெட்வொர்க்கில் பரிவர்த்தனைகளைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்துத் தடை செய்யாது என்ற கொள்கையைக் கொண்டுள்ள THORChain-ன் நிலைப்பாட்டிற்கு இது முற்றிலும் முரணானது.

title: Coinbase receives DCO approval from CFTC, completing full derivatives stack
summary: This completes Coinbase's derivatives infrastructure, allowing it to list, broker, and clear fully collateralized products in-house.
content: Coinbase has received Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) approval from the CFTC. This milestone completes the company's derivatives infrastructure. Coinbase is now fully equipped to list, broker, and clear fully collateralized products entirely in-house, expanding its regulatory capabilities and strengthening its position in the derivatives market.
content_ta: Coinbase நிறுவனத்திற்கு CFTC-யிடமிருந்து Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) ஒப்புதல் கிடைத்துள்ளது. இந்த முக்கிய மைல்கல் மூலம் நிறுவனத்தின் டெரிவேட்டிவ்ஸ் உள்கட்டமைப்பு முழுமையடைந்துள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் Coinbase தனது சொந்த நிறுவனத்திற்குள்ளேயே முழுமையாக ஈடுசெய்யப்பட்ட தயாரிப்புகளை பட்டியலிடவும், தரகு செய்யவுமான அனுமதியைப் பெற்றுள்ளது.

title: Pump.fun: Why PUMP’s 20% surge faces KEY test despite $466M buybacks
summary: Pump.fun’s buybacks strengthened PUMP’s supply narrative as price corrected from the $0.005287 resistance.
content: Pump.fun recently experienced a notable 20 percent surge in its PUMP token, supported by significant buybacks totaling $466 million. However, the token now faces a critical market test as its price experiences a correction after failing to maintain momentum near the $0.005287 resistance level.

title: The Businesses Propping Up Britain’s Local Economy Are Disappearing Fastest Where They Are Needed Most
summary:
Established SMEs (eSMEs) – businesses with 5 to 249 employees that are critical for sustaining local economies – are vanishing fastest in exactly the places that rely on them most, according to new research from Allica Bank.
The report, Good Growth Icons, finds that while the UK’s eSME population is larger today than it was a decade ago, growth has stalled in the past three years and is increasingly concentrated in London.
 
Between 2016 and 2026, eSME numbers increased by just under 7% across the UK, with London accounting for 44% of net growth.
 
But in the past three years all UK regions, with the exception of London and Northern Ireland, have seen eSME numbers decline, with Northern Ireland registering just 0.2% growth (40 businesses).
 
The South West recorded the steepest recent decline of any region, with its eSME base declining by 3.8%, followed by Wales (-3.4%) and the West Midlands (-3.1%).
 
Rural areas are most at risk to the recent decline in eSME numbers
 
The research – based on the Office for National Statistics’ latest UK business counts data –suggests that eSME numbers are disproportionately declining in the areas where they support the greatest share of jobs.
 
In the most rural local authority districts in the UK, eSMEs have declined by 2.3% in the past three years, compared with 1.2% growth in the most urban areas. These urban districts are three times more likely than rural districts to have experienced recent eSME growth.
 
Yet it is these rural areas that rely most heavily on eSMEs for employment, supporting 48% of jobs on average compared with just 33% in the most urban areas.
 
The report identifies certain local authorities that have experienced the sharpest decline in eSME numbers in the past three years, including Erewash (-20%), Wyre Forest (-18%), Stratford-on-Avon (-17%) and Blackpool (-16%).
 
Good growth in every postcode starts here
 
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to deliver "good growth in every postcode” and Allica Bank argues that pledge cannot be met without eSMEs.
 
The UK's 592,500 eSMEs employ around 10.7 million people and generate 37% of private sector turnover. The report estimates there are 16,300 eSMEs in the UK that grew turnover by over 20% in the past year and can make a meaningful contribution to future growth.
 
While these high-growth potential eSMEs are disproportionately concentrated in London, there are 10,700 outside the capital growing at such a rate as to fund significant local investment in all parts of the UK.
 
To back them, Allica Bank is calling on the Government to take four steps:
• A Scale-up Guarantee: Create a new tier of the Growth Guarantee Scheme offering a 70% guarantee on facilities between £2 million and £5 million for high-growth firms that lack tangible assets.
• Support regional skills development: Fully devolve adult skills funding to Strategic Authorities and introduce a Growth & Skills Levy pool, with a focus on developing eSME AI skills.
• Reform business owner taxes: Reduce the cost of doing business for eSMEs and introduce an eSME Reinvestment Relief to encourage business reinvestment.
• Establish regional eSME Growth Forums: Give eSMEs a permanent voice with local leaders to identify barriers to growth and shape Local Growth Plans.
 

Richard Davies, CEO of Allica Bank, said:
"The Prime Minister has pledged to deliver 'good growth in every postcode', and established businesses can make it happen.”
 
“These firms are the engine of regional growth across the UK. They keep local economies running and communities thriving. They may not be the hyper-growth scale-ups that grab the headlines, but they sustain local jobs for decades, often in the very places national growth strategies overlook. We urge the Government to put established businesses at the heart of its growth agenda and its mission to deliver good growth in every postcode.”

title: Ingenico and KSU Open New Fintech Hub
summary:
Ingenico, the smart technology powering in-person commerce, today announced the opening of the Ingenico Fintech Innovation Hub at Kennesaw State University (KSU), the latest investment in its global strategy to develop the next generation of fintech talent.
The Hub builds on a partnership between Ingenico and KSU, which began in late 2024. Nine former KSU interns have since joined Ingenico in full-time roles including software development, quality assurance, technical support, solutions engineering, and project management, demonstrating the program's success in creating pathways from education  into careers in commerce technology.
At the center of the Hub is an Ingenico lab where students can test payment devices in live-use scenarios and gain insight into the technologies shaping modern commerce.
"The future of our industry depends on attracting and developing talented people with the skills to innovate," said Olga Damiron, Chief People Officer, Ingenico. "Our partnership with Kennesaw State University is already delivering results, and this new hub takes that collaboration to the next level by giving students direct exposure to the technologies, challenges and opportunities shaping the future of commerce."
“This all started as a vision, not a finished plan,” said Nick Suppiah, director of Kennesaw State’s Master of Science in Digital Financial Technologies. “I wanted our students to get real, hands-on training that would open doors for them to push financial tech into the future. Along the way, we realized they needed more than a classroom - they needed a place to build. I brought that vision to Ingenico, and it grew from there into something no one fully expected. We don't know exactly what fintech innovations will spark from this lab setting, but that's what makes it exciting. The sky's the limit, and I can't wait to see what our students create."
Students in Suppiah’s project management course played an active role in shaping the Ingenico Fintech Hub. In 2025, a student team, including several participants who have since joined Ingenico, presented concepts to Ingenico’s  leadership. Many of their recommendations were incorporated into the final design.
The KSU partnership is one of several university collaborations supporting Ingenico's global talent strategy. Across North America, Europe and Asia, the company works with leading academic institutions to help students gain practical experience while building a strong pipeline of future engineers, technologists and fintech specialists.
In the Asia-Pacific region, Ingenico collaborates with Maynooth International Engineering College (MIEC), Fuzhou University, Fuzhou, Fujian Province, China. China through a program that has supported 19 internships to date.
Similarly, in Europe, Ingenico's partnership with the Université Grenoble Alpes, in Valence, France have provided opportunities for more than 50 students to to gain industry experience and exposure to the fintech sector at Ingenico, in the past three years.
Together, these partnerships are helping Ingenico build a strong and diverse pipeline of future talent while giving students valuable industry experience.
As commerce continues to evolve, Ingenico remains committed to creating opportunities for the next generation of talent through education, industry collaboration and real-world learning experiences that help shape the future of commerce.

title: HSBC Launch New Digital Solution to Transform Transaction Banking
summary:
HSBC has today announced the next phase of its digital banking transformation with the launch of HSBCnio, a digital solution that simplifies the banking experience for its corporate and institutional clients. HSBCnio brings HSBC’s services, data and intelligence into the channels, platforms and workflows where clients run their businesses. This includes engagement through web and mobile, connecting their systems directly, or using AI tools to access banking information.
By bringing together interactive channels, embedded connectivity and AI interfaces, HSBCnio gives clients a more connected way to bank, including:
Interaction with web and mobile app through a simplified design that provides a clear and consistent experience for viewing cash positions and transactions, trade loans, FX and tracking payments, which makes it easier to access information and identify items that need attention.
Embedded connectivity and APIs, which bring banking services, data and intelligence into clients’ platforms and workflows.
API documentation, software development kits and a sandbox to help reduce integration friction and accelerate the path from development to production.
AI-enabled access through HSBC’s Model Context Protocol, which enables clients’ own AI tools to query authorised account and transaction information and helps teams find and interpret banking data more quickly.

“The new solution brings transaction banking capabilities into the channels and workflows that clients use today, while helping them integrate AI through secure, permissioned access to their banking information.
“AI is core to the design of HSBCnio and supports HSBC’s ambition to build a bank for the future by embedding AI solutions that benefit our clients. We are investing in the technology and platforms needed to serve customers more effectively, enabling them to compare products more quickly and explore a wider range of options.”
Treasury teams increasingly operate across multiple markets, systems and workflows, yet banking access can remain fragmented. HSBCnio addresses that complexity by giving clients a simple, connected way to access transaction banking capabilities, reducing operational friction, supporting automation and providing more timely information for decision-making.
HSBCnio enables clients’ own AI tools to access authorised account and transaction information through HSBC’s Model Context Protocol, while laying the foundation for further AI-enabled experiences within HSBCnio. This helps clients introduce AI into treasury workflows using trusted data, established permissions and appropriate controls. 
HSBC plans to add further transaction banking capabilities and AI-enabled experiences to HSBCnio over time. This includes ‘Ask HSBC’, an AI-enabled experience within HSBCnio designed to help clients query and interpret their banking information.

title: Terrabank Selects TerraPay to Power Cross-Border Pay-to-Account and Digital Wallet Transactions via the Mozrt SmartRails™ Platform

The partnership highlights the sheer scale and speed of TerraPay's infrastructure, which, when paired with Mozrt’s smart routing, unlocks massive global reach for Terrabank's retail, business, correspondent banking, and fintech clients.

title: Trust Becomes the New Cyber Battleground in 2027
summary:
Experian® today released its 2027 Data Breach Industry Forecast: Consumers at Risk, offering a look at the evolving cybersecurity landscape and the growing risks facing consumers and organizations in the years ahead. Now in its 14th year, the annual report explores how artificial intelligence (AI), identity fraud, data breaches and digital deception are converging to create what may become one of the biggest cybersecurity challenges of next year and beyond: a crisis of trust.
As cybercriminals gain access to decades of stolen personal data and increasingly powerful AI tools, businesses may find it harder than ever to verify identities online to combat fraud. At the same time, consumers may face increasing difficulty distinguishing legitimate communications from fraudulent ones and preventing identity doppelgängers. The report examines how these trends could transform the relationship between businesses, consumers and digital trust.
"Organizations have spent years focusing on preventing breaches and securing data. But with decades of exposed data already circulating the focus also needs to be on verification practices, combatting fraud and helping consumers determine what and who they can trust," said Michael Bruemmer, Vice President of Global Data Breach Resolution at Experian. "Cybersecurity is entering a new era where proving authenticity is just as important as protecting data and Experian can help with leading verification and fraud prevention services as well as providing post-incident response support. Businesses that prepare now will be in a stronger position to navigate the evolving threat landscape and maintain customer confidence."
Emerging Trends That Could Shape 2027
The forecast outlines four predictions that examine potential changes and risks on the horizon, including:
Proof of Being Human Becomes the Hottest New Market: The rise of technologies and services designed to help organizations and consumers verify authenticity in an AI-driven world.
The Rise of the Digital Doppelgänger: The evolution of identity theft as cybercriminals build increasingly sophisticated and convincing profiles of individuals.
Consumers Fighting Fire with Fire: New ways consumers may attempt to protect themselves from identity theft as the number of data breaches continues to climb.
Breach Notifications Need a Reset: How growing skepticism toward digital communications could influence regulatory mandates and future data breach notification practices.
Experian Data Breach Resolution helps organizations respond quickly and confidently to data breaches with over 24 years of crisis-management experience. The company's services include breach preparedness, consumer notification, contact center support, identity protection services and global response capabilities designed to help organizations protect customer trust and reduce reputational risk.

Headquartered in London with 2,300 employees worldwide, Checkout.com is increasing its investment both in the UK and internationally. It operates across 56 countries with 10 acquiring licenses and recently announced the US as its fastest growing region, with processing volumes growing over 120% year to date. Checkout.com is also operational with its MALPB charter, enabling direct acquiring in the US – a market which now accounts for 20% of the company’s payment volumes, up from 15% the year before. 
Antoine Nougué, CRO, said: “Reaching $750 million in annualised net revenue is a meaningful milestone, but it is not the finish line. It is the result of staying close to our core: solving the hardest payment problems for the world’s most ambitious merchants and compounding what we learn. Our return to sustained profitability gives us the freedom to invest with conviction through the next decade. AI is at the heart of that investment and our purpose is simple: to help merchants generate more revenue and stay ahead.”

title: Linedata and AutoRek Announce Strategic Partnership to Reshape Asset Management Workflows
summary:
Linedata, a global provider of credit and asset management technology, data, and services, today announced that it was entering a strategic partnership with AutoRek. The agreement makes AutoRek's automated reconciliation platform available to Linedata clients as a fully managed service, delivered through Linedata's co-sourcing model. This partnership will provide Linedata’s clients with market leading reconciliation capability without requiring standalone procurement, implementation or management.
Reconciliation remains one of the most cumbersome processes in investment operations, in need of automation. AutoRek's 2026 research across UK and US capital markets firms found that 85% say their operational processes already struggle, or would struggle, if transaction volumes continue to rise; 53% still use spreadsheets to some extent for reconciliations; and firms spend an average of 15.9% of their operational budgets fixing problems caused by manual processes.1 However, there are barriers to adopting reconciliation, which include licensing, implementation, and staffing.

title: TNS Expands Android Terminal Platform with Bring Your Own App
summary:
Transaction Network Services (TNS) has unveiled its new Bring Your Own App (BYOA) capability. BYOA enables operators to create and deploy their own customer-facing applications on TNS's Android-based unattended payment terminals without having to manage the complexity of payment processing, compliance and certification.
Demand for customized payment experiences has grown in recent years and payment operators are looking for ways to innovate without taking on the complexity of payment application development, PCI compliance requirements, certifications, security obligations, and ongoing maintenance. TNS’s BYOA removes that trade-off by enabling operators to develop and deploy their own Android applications on TNS-supported unattended, retail and fuel payment terminals while TNS manages payment processing, PCI compliance requirements, payment and P2PE certifications, and the supporting payment infrastructure.
Using a flexible integrated model, BYOA provides a customized payment experience by:
Allowing the operator’s Android application to call the TNS payment application on the terminal through a defined payments API to initiate the transaction
TNS handling card capture, PIN collection, encryption, EMV processing and payment certification
Each operator application is signed and approved by TNS before it can run on the terminal
This model provides developers with a clean integration point to innovate on the customer experience without inheriting the usual security and compliance burden.
"Operators have historically had to choose between innovating on customer experience or taking on the complexity of payments,” said David Hore, Senior Director, Payments Product Portfolio, TNS Payments Market. “BYOA is designed to remove that compromise. Our customers can build the applications that enhance their business’ unique selling proposition (USP), while we manage the payments, compliance and certification that sit behind every transaction. That's the role TNS plays – providing a managed service that allows our customers to focus on their business."
Beyond customer experience innovation, BYOA also simplifies ongoing payment operations. Its decoupled architecture separates acquirer keys from terminal keys, enabling operators to switch acquirers or revise rates without updating physical terminals – providing greater flexibility while reducing operational burden.
"This is exactly the kind of flexibility unattended operators need to meet the demands of the modern payments landscape," said Michael Johnson, Global Managing Director, Payments Market Business, TNS. "BYOA gives customers the freedom to create differentiated experiences that reflect their brand and their customers' needs, backed by a payments foundation they can trust."

title: One Repair Away from Crisis: Quarter of UK Drivers Have No Money Set Aside for Vehicle Emergencies
summary:
With households already stretched by the cost of food, energy and other essentials, new research suggests millions of UK drivers are just one fault away from a financial shock.
Four in ten (40%) UK drivers say they could not afford an unexpected car repair costing more than £249 without cutting back elsewhere, borrowing money, using credit or delaying another bill. Yet the average cost of a car repair can reach up to £700*,leaving drivers facing a potential shortfall of almost three times what they say they could comfortably afford. 
New research commissioned by subscription lender Creditspring among 1,273 UK drivers found that a quarter (25%) have no money put aside specifically for vehicle emergencies, leaving many with nowhere to turn when a fault strikes.
Car emergency not a factor
For many, this isn’t simply a question of willingness. Nearly one in seven drivers (14%) say they cannot afford to save regularly for costs like this, while a similar proportion have simply not thought about it. Others (8%) say they are happy to take a chance on nothing going wrong.
Yet, when a repair bill does arrive, drivers are most likely to turn to savings (29%) or a credit card (19%) to cover it – both of which come with their own trade-offs. Savings are often put away with a goal in mind and can leave people with even less of a buffer for what comes next, while paying by credit card can mean the true cost of a repair grows the longer it takes to pay off.
Drivers plan for the predictable costs, not the ones that cause a crisis
The research suggests many drivers aren’t fully considering the right budgeting when it comes to their vehicles. Car insurance (46%), MOT (42%) and road tax (42%) are all front of mind and the annual costs drivers say they plan for most, but the costs more likely to catch someone out sit much further down the list. 
Unexpected repairs (20%), breakdown and recovery (23%) and parking (12%) are elements that drivers aren’t factoring into budgets. With research suggesting that the average driver’s parking bill per year is £260*1, the gap between what drivers plan for and what actually derails them could leave many exposed exactly when it matters most.
That unpredictability is already colouring how drivers feel about routine motoring costs. One in seven (14%) say an MOT or service feels like a “financial lottery”, while 17% worry that a routine check could uncover a repair bill they cannot afford - a sign that anxiety about car costs often sets in long before anything actually goes wrong.
The same £500, but not the same stress
The disconnect goes further than budgeting habits. When asked to name their most stressful one-off cost, Brits agreed that a £500 increase in energy bills was more unsettling than an unexpected £500 car repair, despite the two carrying an identical price tag. It suggests many drivers do not weigh up car costs in the same way as other household bills, even when the numbers are the same, perhaps because a repair feels unplanned, or more like bad luck than a bill. 
Tamsin Powell, Consumer Finance Expert at Creditspring, said: “An unexpected repair bill is rarely just about the car. It can mean worrying about whether there is enough left for food, energy, rent or the bills that are already due.
“For households already balancing a tight budget, a fault can leave people feeling they have to choose between keeping the car on the road and protecting everything else. That is why a relatively modest repair bill can feel so disruptive.
“You cannot plan for every breakdown. But you can make the shock more manageable by knowing the costs that are coming, putting aside what you can, and getting clear information before making a decision under pressure.”
Tamsin shares her tips for managing unexpected car costs:
Start small with a separate vehicle buffer: If you can, put aside a realistic amount each month for car costs. A modest buffer can still create more options when a fault appears. If you don’t end up using it during the year, you can add it to your savings instead.
Map out known costs across the year: Make a note of when insurance, tax, MOT and servicing are due, then divide the likely cost into monthly amounts. This helps distinguish the bills you can plan for from the ones you cannot. It is important to factor in items like parking and road charges too where possible as smaller costs can all add up.  
Do not ignore warning signs: A dashboard light, unusual noise or change in how the car drives can be easy to postpone. Seeking advice early may give you more time to understand the issue and compare options before the problem gets even more expensive.
Ask the garage for a clear breakdown: Request an itemised quote, ask which work is essential for safety and roadworthiness, and find out whether any repairs can be prioritised. If the work is not urgent, consider getting another quote.
Pause before using credit: If borrowing is necessary, look at the total amount repayable, the repayment dates and what the repayments will mean alongside existing bills. The right option is one you can afford to repay without creating another problem.

title: Plumery Launches DBP Rescue Plan to Help Financial Institutions Break Free from Vendor Lock-In
summary:
Plumery, the digital banking development platform, today launched its DBP Rescue Plan, a global programme designed to move financial institutions away from digital banking platforms (DBP) that are no longer meeting their needs. The initiative is available to 10 financial institutions on a first–come, first served basis, with Plumery aiming to complete all migrations within 12 months. 
Moving away from a digital banking platform can feel harder than staying locked into one that has become increasingly difficult or costly to adapt. Agreed implementation timelines can slip under existing contracts, custom development can come at a high cost without the institution owning what is built, and major upgrades can bring significant new bills.
Accenture’s 2026 banking trends research found that around 70% of banks’ IT budgets go to maintaining technical debt, while software costs have grown approximately 8% annually since 2017, outpacing banking revenue. In some cases, upgrading an existing platform can even cost more than building it from scratch. 
The DBP Rescue Plan is designed to remove the barriers to migration, giving banks a defined path to move away from their existing platform without taking on the full risk and cost of switching platforms. Participating banks will receive a specialist migration team, proven tooling and playbooks, and a Proof of Migration framework that allows institutions to test the migration against their own environment, systems and requirements before committing to the programme. Once they make the switch, institutions can move beyond vendor dependency and build with greater flexibility and speed, giving their teams more control over how their digital banking capabilities evolve.
“Too many financial institutions stay with digital banking platforms that are no longer working for them because leaving feels riskier than staying,” said Ben Goldin, CEO at Plumery. “The DBP Rescue Plan is designed to remove some of that risk. By combining migration expertise, proven tooling and a commercial model that removes software licensing costs for up to two years during the transition, we’re giving institutions a practical way to move forward and take back control over their digital future. Now the real risk is staying.”
The DBP rescue plan
The programme is open to financial institutions looking to move away from their existing digital banking platform and regain control over their technology roadmap. The first ten institutions to join will receive: 
No additional software licenses: Plumery will provide software licenses at no cost for up to 24 months so you don’t pay double when the existing contract runs out. Standard commercial terms apply after the free license period. 
Ownership of roadmap: Institutions retain ownership of what is built, rather than paying for custom capabilities. Plumery’s headless, BIAN-based architecture provides a flexible, standardised foundation for their teams, system integrators and AI agents to build on directly, without relying on a vendor’s roadmap. This gives institutions greater control over how their digital banking capabilities evolve whilst enabling them to accelerate innovation, support growth and keep pace with their competitors.
A migration path, not a leap of faith: Plumery’s migration playbooks and tooling are designed to provide a defined path from the existing platform to the new environment, with specialist team members having helped build and migrate platforms for more than 100 banks worldwide.
Outcome-based delivery: Delivery milestones are agreed with each institution upfront, with Plumery invoicing only when a milestone has been completed and signed off. This means Plumery shares the delivery risk, with no invoice if an agreed milestone is not delivered.   
Financial institutions can start by booking a Proof of Migration, giving them the opportunity to test the migration approach against their own environment before committing to the programme. This provides a practical way to assess the feasibility of migration before entering into a longer-term agreement.

title: Brite Payments Launches Pay by Bank in the UK as Research Reveals Almost Half of Brits Are Suffering Checkout Rage When Shopping Online
summary:
As Brite Payments brings its cross-border Pay by Bank service to the UK after securing its Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence from the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), new research from the European payments leader reveals just how much of a toll checkout chaos is having on British merchants and consumers. 
A survey of 2,000 UK adults, conducted by market research firm Appinio on behalf of Brite Payments, found that almost half (47%)* of shoppers suffer checkout rage when shopping online, with 1 in 6 having sworn and shouted at the screen. Almost a quarter (24%) have avoided a purchase altogether because of returns anxiety with 15% admitting to buying less so less money would be tied up if they needed a refund. 
Checkout chaos costing merchants
For some Brits, a bad checkout experience is enough for them to end a relationship with a merchant entirely: almost 1 in 5 (19%) said they’d actively blacklist a retailer with poor payment options, and 17% admitted to warning their friends and family away from certain retailers, extending the reputational damage further. 
Elsewhere in the findings, almost a quarter (23%) said they’ve abandoned a purchase entirely to avoid finding their physical card with the average Brit losing an hour a year filling in checkout forms. Scale that across the UK's banked adult population and it becomes the equivalent of losing over 55 million hours** – or more than 6,400 years – on unnecessary payment admin every year.
The friction doesn't ease once a shopper has entered their details, either. A quarter (25%) of shoppers have had a payment fail due to an input error, an expired card or a security check glitch; friction that causes just under 1 in 10 shoppers to switch to another retailer for an easier experience.
Six years in the making
Brite Payments has spent the past six years proving that a faster, more convenient online payment solution exists. Since launching its Pay by Bank business in 2019, the company has built a network connecting more than 3,800 banks across 27 European markets to simplify the instant payment and payout experience, a key driver in combating checkout rage and returns anxiety that shoppers report today. 
With its UK operating licence, the company will begin a phased product roll out, bringing that same proven technology and expertise to British merchants and consumers. Through a single API integration, UK businesses will be able to accept Pay by Bank payments both domestically and across Brite Payments’ European network, all without having to juggle local providers, deal with legacy contracts or wait on slow settlement times. 
The launch also comes at a time when more than 60% of shoppers from the Brite Payments survey say they'd rather use a payment provider that isn't at risk of disruption caused by problems in another country, and 58% would actively choose a UK or European company over an overseas alternative. 
Connecting Europe through faster payments
The UK has more open banking users than almost anywhere in Europe, over 15 million and rising. Brite Payments’ survey shows that knowledge of Pay by Bank is high, with 76% of Brits saying they were familiar with it. Yet its infrastructure has failed to keep up because enterprise merchants keep hitting the same operational ceiling. 
Many legacy account-to-account (A2A) providers were built to serve a single market and, as such, struggle with fragmented technical standards between markets, inconsistent settlement times, and support infrastructure that shows the cracks as soon as transaction volumes and geographic complexity increase. 
Brite Payments has arrived to challenge this status quo. 
“The UK is one of the most mature open banking markets in the world, but it’s been dominated by overseas card networks and reliance on legacy providers built for a single market. Both merchants and consumers are not just losing out, but are actively impacted, as our survey results show,” said Brite Payments’ founder and CEO, Lena Hackelöer. “Today's launch is an exciting moment in a post-Brexit world, as UK merchants can easily start offering Pay by Bank to their local customers and customers across Europe, enabling their expansion internationally.”
UK businesses interested in unlocking the future of payments in the UK and across Europe can learn more at Brite Payments and be the first to benefit.
